translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
To those in Colossae, holy and faithful brothers and sisters in Jesus Christ: Peace and grace to you from God our Father.
We always give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and pray for you,
ever since we heard of your faith in Jesus Christ and your love for all the holy ones,
because of the hope kept for you in heaven, which you heard about beforehand in the message of truth, the good news,
which was proclaimed to you, as it was also to the whole world. It is growing and bearing fruit, just as it has among you since the day you heard and truly came to know the grace of God,
as you learned from Epaphras, our dear companion, who is a faithful servant of Christ on your behalf.
He also told us about your love in the Spirit.
For this reason, since the day we heard, we too have not stopped praying for you and asking that you be filled with the knowledge of God's will in all wisdom and all spiritual understanding,
so that you may live as you should and please God in every good deed, bearing fruit and growing in the knowledge of God.
May you be strengthened with every kind of strength according to the greatness of his glory, with complete endurance and patience, and with joy
give thanks to God the Father, who has made us worthy to share in the inheritance of the holy ones in the light.
He rescued us from the authority of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
in whom we have redemption and forgiveness of sins.
He is the image of the invisible God and the firstborn of all creation.
In him everything in heaven and on earth was created, everything visible and invisible, whether thrones, lordships, rulers, or authorities. Everything was created through him and in him.
He is before everything, and everything holds together in him.
He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning and the firstborn from the dead, so that he may be first in everything,
for all the fullness was pleased to dwell in him.
And through him to reconcile everything to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross—through him—whether things on earth or things in heaven.
You too, who formerly were strangers and enemies in your minds because of your evil deeds, he has now reconciled
in his physical body and through his death, to present you before him holy, without blemish and without accusation,

if you continue in your faith with your foundation firm, without being moved away from the hope of the good news that you heard, which was proclaimed throughout all creation under heaven, and of which I, Paul, became a servant.
And I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions, for the sake of his body, which is the church.
I became its servant according to the stewardship from God that was given to me among you, to fulfill the word of God.
The mystery that was hidden for ages and generations has now been revealed to his holy ones,
to whom God wished to make known how rich is the glory of this mystery among the nations: Christ in you, the hope of our glory.
We proclaim him, teaching and giving understanding to everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone complete in Jesus Christ.
For this I also labor and struggle, with the help of the power given to me.
But I want you to know what a struggle I have for you, for those in Laodicea, and for all the others who have not seen my face in person.

So that their hearts may be encouraged and they may be drawn together in love, into all the riches of full assurance and into the understanding of the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ.
In him all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
I say this so that no one may mislead you with persuasive words.
For although I am separated from you in body, I am with you in spirit, and I rejoice to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
Therefore, just as you received Jesus Christ our Lord, live in him,
with your roots firmly established, being built up in him and strengthened in the faith you learned, so that in it you may overflow with thanksgiving.
Be careful that no one carries you off through philosophy and empty deception, according to human teachings and the elements of the world, rather than according to Christ.
For in him the whole fullness of divinity dwells bodily.
And in him you too have been made complete. He is the head of all rulers and authorities.
In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not performed by hands, by stripping off the flesh of sins through the circumcision of Christ.
You were buried with him in baptism, and in it you also rose with him, because you believed in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.
And you, who were dead in your sins and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive with him, and he forgave us all our sins.
Through his commandments he erased the written record of our debts, which stood against us. He removed it from our midst and nailed it to his cross.
By stripping off his body, he exposed the rulers and authorities and publicly put them to shame in his own person.
Therefore, let no one trouble you about food and drink, or about distinctions concerning festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths.
These are shadows of things to come, but the body is Christ.

Do not let anyone seek to condemn you under the guise of humility, so that you become subject to the worship of angels. Such a person ventures into what he has not seen and is vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind.
He does not hold firmly to the head, from whom the whole body is joined together and sustained through its sinews and limbs, and grows with the growth that comes from God.
For if you died with Christ to the elements of the world, why do you submit to rules as though you were still living in the world?
They say, “Do not approach, do not taste, and do not handle.”
These concern things that perish with use, and they are human commandments and teachings.
They appear to contain some wisdom, with a show of humility and reverence for God and of not sparing the body—not in anything honorable, but in things that serve the needs of the flesh.
Therefore, if you have risen with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on the things above, not on the things on earth.
For you have died, and your lives are hidden with Christ in God.
And when Christ, who is our life, is revealed, then you too will be revealed with him in glory.
Therefore put to death your earthly members: sexual immorality, impurity, passions, evil desire, and greed, which is idol worship.
For because of these things, God's wrath is coming upon the disobedient.
You too once walked in these ways, when you lived in them.
But now put all these things away from you: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy speech.
Do not lie to one another. Instead, strip off the old self with all its practices,
and put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the likeness of its Creator,
where there is neither Jew nor Aramean, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision, neither Greek nor barbarian, neither slave nor free person, but Christ is everything and is in everyone.
Therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with compassion, tenderness, kindness, humility of mind, gentleness, and patience.
And bear with one another and forgive one another. If anyone has a complaint against another, forgive just as Christ forgave you.
And along with all these things, put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
Let the peace of Christ guide your hearts, for you were called to it in one body. And give thanks to Christ,
so that his word may dwell richly in you in all wisdom. Teach and instruct one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, and sing to God with gratitude in your hearts.
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks through him to God the Father.
Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in Christ.
Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter toward them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the sight of our Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, so that they do not become discouraged.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only when they are watching, like those who seek to please people, but with a sincere heart and in the fear of the Lord.
And whatever you do, do it with your whole soul, as for our Lord and not for people.
And know that you will receive from our Lord the reward of an inheritance, for you serve the Lord Christ.
But the wrongdoer will be repaid according to the wrong he has done, and there is no favoritism.
Masters, treat your slaves with fairness and justice, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.
Persevere in prayer, remaining watchful in it and giving thanks.
And pray for us too, that God may open a door for us to speak the message, to declare the mystery of Christ, for whose sake I am imprisoned,
so that I may reveal it and speak of it as I ought.
Conduct yourselves wisely toward outsiders, and make the most of your opportunities.
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned as if with salt, so that you know how you ought to answer each person.
Tychicus, our beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will tell you about my circumstances.
I have sent him to you for this very purpose: to learn about your circumstances and encourage your hearts,
along with Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother who is one of you. They will tell you about our circumstances.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends you greetings, as does Mark, Barnabas's cousin. You received instructions about him: if he comes to you, welcome him.
And Jesus, who is called Justus. These are of the circumcision, and they alone helped me in the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, sends you greetings. He is always laboring for you in prayer, so that you may stand mature and complete in all the will of God.
For I testify about him that he has great zeal for you and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Luke, our beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings.
Greet the brothers in Laodicea, Nymphas, and the church in his house.
When this letter has been read among you, arrange for it to be read also in the church of the Laodiceans. And you yourselves should read the letter written from Laodicea.
Tell Archippus, “Pay attention to the ministry you received in our Lord, so that you fulfill it.”
This greeting is in my own hand, Paul's. Remember my chains. Grace be with you. Amen.
